title: introduce cost_suggester client and presets-wizard for batching/caching/quant
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: teams building against Redwood need automated, repeatable suggestions for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization so they can reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This PR adds a first-class cost_suggester client to the Python SDK plus a lightweight presets-wizard CLI that walks a user through generating recommended defaults for a given workload signature.

What changed (single-line summary): added SDK surface, CLI helper, unit/integration tests, and docs/examples. The changes are feature-flagged behind 'cost_suggester' to allow staged rollout.

Design notes: the SDK exposes CostSuggester.suggest_profiles(workload_signature: str, sample_stats: dict, constraints: dict) -> List[Preset] (Python typing in code). The backend call returns ranked profiles for batch_size, cache_ttl_ms, quant_profile (fp16/int8 variants), and an estimated unit-econ delta (pct). The presets-wizard CLI wraps the call and renders an interactive YAML preset file that can be dropped into a service config. Safety: the client applies a conservative fallback when live telemetry is unavailable and marks profiles 'suggested' not 'applied' by default. Rollout plan: feature-flag + beta docs; we will promote to GA after 2 customer trials and no major regressions in 2 weeks.

Checklist: 
- [x] SDK surface and docs
- [x] CLI presets-wizard with non-interactive mode
- [x] Unit tests covering mapping logic and edge cases
- [x] Integration test that runs against recorded replay dataset (small)
- [x] Telemetry tagging for prescriptive recommendations
- [x] Feature-flag guard

Backward compatibility: default client behavior is unchanged unless the new CostSuggester class is instantiated. No breaking changes to existing endpoint clients.

Notes for reviewers: prioritize API ergonomics and error handling (timeouts/circuit-breakers). I included an example in examples/cost_presets/ that demonstrates migrating from naive defaults to suggested presets.

Related: ENG-1432 for estimator design, PM-88 for UX spec.
